deck_context.source_summary: Week 03 teaches students to read a two-loop Kirchhoff matrix as a compact representation of physical equations before solving in MATLAB.
deck_context.core_claim: A coefficient is trustworthy only when its value, sign, matrix position, and physical origin agree.

slides.title: Audit the matrix before asking MATLAB to solve
slides.intent: Correct only the semantic mapping arrows while preserving the current student-facing slide copy and content.
key_points: Every coefficient should read back as physics.
Check the value, the sign, and the physical origin of each matrix entry before solving in MATLAB.

required_images.role: approved revised Week 03 sample slide style reference
required_images.fidelity: match style only; do not copy exact layout or content
preserve the title, 2x2 coefficient matrix, audit table, matrix values, signs, units, physical-origin text, and the existing lower takeaway; edit only the connector arrows and their source anchors
preserve A11=3 Ω, A12=−1 Ω, A21=−1 Ω, A22=4 Ω and every physical-origin statement exactly

slides.layout: retain the current matrix-left and table-right composition; reserve a clean connector gutter between them and keep the original bottom takeaway
slides.visual_elements: four independent colour-matched semantic arrows map A11→row 1, A12→row 2, A21→row 3, and A22→row 4
slides.source_image_rules: Use the current Slide 06 as the edit base. Use the audit table as a strict source. The arrows are semantic entry-to-row mapping arrows, not circuit-current arrows.
constraints: A11→row 1, A12→row 2, A21→row 3, and A22→row 4. Every arrowhead must point into the matching Entry-column row beside the correct entry label, never toward the Value or Physical origin columns.
Use four separate source dots on the correct cells. A21 must start on the A21 cell's top edge; it must never start on A22 or share A22's anchor. A22 must start on the A22 cell's bottom edge.

Follow this geometry exactly: A11 rises from its top edge to the row-1 centreline then travels right; A12 is a straight horizontal arrow; A21 rises from its top edge, travels above A22 to the gutter, drops to row 3, then turns right; A22 drops below the matrix then travels right along row 4.
Use separate paths, one arrowhead per path, and no shared segments, shared junctions, crossings, or contact with another coefficient cell.

If the table border blocks the arrowhead, place a small matching target dot inside the left half of the corresponding Entry cell and terminate the arrowhead at that dot; do not stop ambiguously at the outer table border.
Keep the semantic colour map: blue for A11/A22, ochre for A12, sage for A21. Matching cell, coefficient number, connector, target, and row tint must use the same colour.

Preserve the existing student-facing lower takeaway exactly: Every coefficient should read back as physics. Check the value, the sign, and the physical origin of each matrix entry before solving in MATLAB.

Do not add a bullet list of equations, internal production instructions, arrow explanations, new captions, or any other new copy. No slide number, outer frame, watermark, unrelated logo, or altered numerical content.
